title: How much does repeating the oracle actually buy, and what does it cost?
hypothesis: k=3 majority voting removes most of the v8 prompt's run-to-run randomness. The quantity that matters is not the flip RATE but how often a k-majority differs from the verdict an infinitely-repeated oracle would give.
subject: human_thriving v8 prompt, both arms

population.note: Phase A cohort, design-weighted; boundary ~4.4x oversampled

decision_rationale: k=3 adopted. The curve flattens because the residual is rows with no stable oracle answer, which no k removes; k=5 fixes ~33 rows of 6,590.
review: 3 lenses (adversarial, claim-verification, doc-accuracy) + a 4th on the rewrite. Revision 1 had 3 blockers: its headline validation was an algebraic identity (pairwise disagreement is exactly 2/3 x non-unanimity over 3 draws), it compared a production-mix gate figure to a boundary label figure, and its cost multipliers were draw counts. All corrected in revision 2; two further errors found after that.
notes: Estimand is self-consistency, not accuracy: the limit verdict is the oracle's own central tendency, not ground truth. Cost figures were superseded by EXP-004. Inputs staged 2026-08-30 at b650-gpu:~/v8_corpus/experiment_inputs/ (phaseA/ and cache_ttl/), verified by sha256; they had been in tmpfs only.

title: Does the v8.1 prompt fix Gate B-A, and what does each clause cost?
hypothesis: Acceptance criterion 1 fails because the nursery row scores 4.400 against a 3.85 bar. Four v8.1 clauses were written from owner rulings; measure Gate B-A, the no-regression control, and each clause in isolation.
subject: prompt-v8-1.md (32bbbdb68f38), prompt-v8-1b.md (9b71ba58e0c0) and four single-clause ablations against prompt-candidate-tail.md (003cd35a5122)

population.note: balance probed before the first call (7.40 -> 7.23). Run inside the 06:00-10:00 UTC peak window, deliberately. Article text for all 13 rows is already tracked in datasets/adverse.

decision_rationale: ⛔ The premise was wrong: at k=6 under the UNCHANGED v8 prompt the nursery row is 3.608 sd 2.560 -- a PASS. Criterion 1 was never stably failing; 4.400 was a k=3 mean on a 50/50 bimodal row whose standard error at k=3 is 1.48 against a 0.55 margin. v8.1 is therefore a label-quality change, not an unblocking fix -- and more valuable for it, because B_commence removes the coin toss (1.017 sd 0.055). Clauses B, C and D are stable and move nothing else. A is REJECTED as written: the ablation shows it is the sole cause of a regression on the #91 origin row. PART 2: the four clauses are NOT additive -- each individually safe, their union scores the #91 origin row 5.921 with 12/12 in_scope. Leave-one-out isolates a BxD interaction; D held the only sentence that licenses a positive. SHIPPED prompt-v8-4.md = B + C + A3, D dropped, validated at k=12: Gate B-A 9/9, worst class-A sd 2.250 -> 0.205, in_scope runs on class A 3 -> 0, no-regression 4/4. A placebo of +996 chars of section-1 restatement left the origin row at 0.883 sd 0.037, refuting length and location as the cause.
notes: Three errors of mine, all one root: I wrote commencement as a NECESSARY condition when the ruling made it SUFFICIENT; I then declared that fix successful from a k=3 draw that had sampled 3 stable runs out of a 2-in-6 bimodal distribution; and I read 4/4-same-sign drift on the controls as systematic when paired k=6 gives -0.077. On a bimodal row a k=3 mean is a sample of a coin flip. Gate B-A's k must be re-derived before Phase D. The mechanism inside clause A -- probably its 'Lebanon abolishes death penalty' contrast example -- is a hypothesis, not a measurement. Two more of mine: I validated the union by its parts, and I named the contrast example as the cause from reading before the placebo and A3 refuted it. Generalisable: a rule stated as a TEST inside a reasoning step becomes a question asked of every article; the same rule as a CATEGORY in an exclusion list does not.

title: Train human_thriving v8, and find out whether the checkpoint-selection metric was ever live
hypothesis: Phase C step 1: train the student on labels_v84_merged.jsonl. Sub-question that emerged mid-run: --select-metric was accepted but produced no needle metrics, so selection fell back to aggregate MAE. Does correcting it change which epoch ships, and is the resulting checkpoint better?
subject: google/gemma-3-1b-pt + LoRA r=16 alpha=32, 6 epochs, batch 8, lr 2e-5, max_length 512, seed 42. Two arms differing ONLY in checkpoint selection: MAE (pre-fix, epoch 6) vs recall_medium at 4.5 (post-fix, epoch 4).
oracle: deepseek-chat (labels only; no oracle calls in this experiment)

population.label_provenance: HYBRID: 6130 rows at v8/k=3 (prompt-candidate-tail.md, 003cd35a5122) + 456 above-op rows re-scored at v8.4/k=6 (prompt-v8-4.md, c4705408c477)
population.note: Splits are gitignored (article text at corpus scale, #97). Trained on b650-gpu, CUDA, venv-prodparity.

decision_rationale: The model is trained and the selection defect is fixed, but the two arms are NOT DISTINGUISHABLE and the experiment's headline finding is about the instrument, not the model. Correcting selection DID change the shipped epoch (6 -> 4), refuting the reading -- mine -- that a monotonically falling MAE meant no recall turn had occurred; that inference used MAE to reason about recall, the exact substitution the defect is about. But recall_medium SATURATES at 0.5806 across epochs 4/5/6, so the strict '>' tie-break chose the epoch, not the metric (#144). On the untouched test split epoch 4 leads at 4.5 by two articles on recall and two on specificity, epoch 6 leads on BOTH at 4.25, and they split at 4.0 -- a model that changes rank with a 0.25 threshold move is not distinguishable. Reinforced by seed-42 runs not being bit-reproducible (epoch 6 val MAE 0.5601 vs 0.5605). Epoch 4 kept because it was chosen by a criterion the project endorses, not because it measured better.
review: /review-changes, 4 lenses (reachability, adversarial, claim-verification, doc-accuracy): 4 blockers, 12 warnings, all fixed or filed before the commit was amended.
notes: WEIGHTS ARE NOT ON DISK HERE. adapter_model.safetensors is gitignored and lives only at b650-gpu:~/llm-distillery/filters/human_thriving/v8/model/ (epoch 4) with the MAE-selected arm at model_baseline_mae/ (epoch 6). The committed history/metadata are the provenance; the weights are not reproducible from this repo. The two metadata files use the PRE-AMEND schema (select_metric / select_metric_available / medium_threshold); 1878e7b writes requested_* plus checkpoint-scoped fields, so a future run's file will not match these key-for-key. The checkpoint was produced by the tree that became 1878e7b via an amend, so its exact sha (0697f5a) is dangling; 1878e7b resolves this filter to the same 4.5 and does not change recall_at_k at n=658, so the numbers reproduce, but the artifact was not built by any commit now on a branch. Calibration and the Stage-1 probe are NOT done -- these are raw uncalibrated student outputs and Phase C is incomplete.

title: Phase C part 2 for human_thriving v8: retrain the Stage-1 probe and fit calibration -- do either move recall?
hypothesis: v8 was trained but could not score: no base_scorer, no inference module, no probe, no calibration.json. Raw test recall at 4.5 was 0.514, below all six deployed filters. The plan aims the probe and the calibration at that number. Build both, then measure whether either moves it.
subject: intfloat/multilingual-e5-small + MLPProbe, --objective recall --target-fn 0.02 --seed 42 --device cpu; per-dimension isotonic calibration fitted on the 658-row val split. Student is EXP-015's epoch-4 checkpoint.
oracle: deepseek-chat (labels only; no oracle calls in this experiment)

population.design_weights: corpus.jsonl inclusion_probability, 0.0341-0.8571 across 17 cells; class-A cells oversampled ~20x. Weighted figures are Horvitz-Thompson estimates for the DRAWABLE population, which EXCLUDES news.google.com (22.1% of production).
population.note: Everything ran on b650-gpu, CPU, venv-prodparity (production pins). CPU chosen so calibration and the mandated Phase D gate device agree; production serves on GPU, so the shipped calibration carries the documented CPU->CUDA 0.1956 term.

decision_rationale: Both artifacts ship and NEITHER MOVED THE TARGET NUMBER. The probe is recall-safe (0 FN at the adopted 1.75 on both splits) so Stage 1 is not what limits recall; the calibration is, measurably, THE SAME RANKER as raw -- Spearman 0.9977, 1.95% discordant pairs, AUC 0.9474 -> 0.9488, and every matched-flag-count recall difference is <=2 articles with inconsistent sign. Its apparent 14-point recall drop at a fixed 4.5 is a THRESHOLD effect: isotonic compresses the top of the scale, so 4.5 calibrated flags 17 rows where 4.5 raw flags 26. The gate's own #95 bands overlap on recall, specificity and F1 -- NOT DISTINGUISHABLE -- so the drop is not reportable as an effect either way. Calibration ships on ADR-008 plus ADR-023's specificity tie-break, explicitly not because it improved anything: on the untouched test split it makes MAE worse in 5 of 6 dimensions (nature_recovery v4's improved test MAE by 22.2%). The threshold 1.75 was chosen against the owner's 2026-08-28 hold-near-pass-through ruling rather than from the script's FN-budget rule, which picked 2.825 and would have cut routing to ~0.52.
notes: THE KEEPER: the Stage-1 threshold belongs to the PROBE, not to the recipe. Seed 7 -- same data, same objective, same code, 0 FN, a BETTER val BCE -- gives a probe on which the configured 1.75 routes 0.7406/0.7567 instead of 0.8876/0.8935, a ~14 pp collapse in Stage-2 routing with every recall number unchanged. Stage 1 is silent by design, so this has no symptom. Guarded: config.yaml records probe_sha256 BESIDE the threshold and inference_hybrid.py refuses to construct on a mismatch; deliberately a different pin from probe/*.pkl.sha256, which travels with the probe and a retrain regenerates. SECOND: hashing is the wrong reproducibility test. Two seed-42 runs are bit-identical in CONTENT (all six tensors np.array_equal, scaler identical) but differ in 134 of 541,144 pickle bytes -- torch storage keys derived from memory addresses -- so sha256sum would have reported 'not reproducible' for a fully reproducible artifact. THIRD: probes shipped before today were UNSEEDED; --seed was added and is now recorded in the pickle's metrics. FOURTH: fit_calibration.py's default edits config.yaml with score_scale_factor = 10/weighted_max; here 1.3787, which with no normalization.json would stretch every score 1.38x. Added --no-config-update, proven by an unchanged config sha256. It is opt-in, so any filter fitted before its normalization still gets the edit. FIFTH, an open gap: the routing asymmetry between Latin and non-Latin is real (6.93 pp, z=2.53) but the FN half is unmeasurable at 8 non-Latin positives -- rule-of-three upper bound 0.375. '0 FN in every script cell' is true and nearly uninformative; the instrument could not have said otherwise. #141 is the blocker. SIXTH, found by the review battery not by me and worth its own line: the routing-gap significance test shipped UNWEIGHTED inside an evidence directory whose thesis is that a sample rate describes no population, because Sigma-w was not recorded per group and so a weighted rate could not be pooled across splits. Recording it (sum_weights*) and redoing the test made the gap LARGER -- 0.0762 weighted against 0.0693 unweighted, z 2.65 vs 2.53 -- so the finding was never at risk and the reporting was. Both SEs are still binomial and therefore optimistic on a stratified design; measured Kish deff 1.068 moves the unweighted z to 2.45. SEVENTH: probe_recall_report.py promised in its own --corpus help text and in the JSON's design_weight_note that weighted columns were 'omitted rather than silently computed with weight 1', and emitted them unconditionally -- the field is there, is populated, and is a different instrument from the one its name claims. EIGHTH: dump_student_scores.py's presence control raised AFTER writing and closing all three output files, so the files it 'refused to emit' were on disk. NINTH: the no-prefilter refusal in base_scorer.py was UNREACHABLE on the hybrid path, because HybridScorer._create_stage2_scorer hardcodes use_prefilter=False -- a documented refusal that could not fire, which is the shape it was written to prevent. TENTH: 'every other inference_hybrid.py hardcodes DEFAULT_THRESHOLD = 1.00' was asserted on six surfaces and is true of 2 of 13; worse, the claim's own next clause ('they agree today, so it is harmless') is refuted by nature_recovery v4, which ships config 3.225 against runtime 0.75.

title: Did Phase C work? — and is v8's recall comparable to the fleet's at all?
hypothesis: Phase C was written up as a disappointment: recall 0.486/0.343 against a deployed fleet at 0.59-0.72, with calibration 'not distinguishable'. Both readings depend on comparisons nobody had checked. Test (a) whether v7 and v8 share a positive class at all, and (b) whether the trained student does the thing v8 exists to do -- stop surfacing what v7 wrongly surfaced.
subject: The EXP-016 single forward pass over the 660-row test split (raw and calibrated arms), joined to each row's v7_score from corpus.jsonl. No new inference.
oracle: deepseek-chat (labels only; no oracle calls in this experiment)

population.note: Every row carries a v7_score; the script refuses to run if any is missing, because a partial join would silently shrink the disputed set. Held-out: the split was untouched by training, checkpoint selection, the probe and the calibration fit.

decision_rationale: Phase C worked, and the metric it was judged on could not show it. (a) THE FLEET COMPARISON IS VOID: v7 and v8 do not share a positive class -- 117 vs 35 positives on the same 660 rows, agreeing on 30, Jaccard 0.246. Recall is conditional on the true class, which is why it survives a change of base RATE and not a change of DEFINITION; 'v8's recall is below all six' compared two different quantities that share a name, and it had been propagated to six surfaces. (b) AGAINST ITS ACTUAL PURPOSE v8 succeeds: of the 87 test rows v7 surfaced that the v8 oracle demotes, the student removes 90.8% raw / 94.3% calibrated, at a cost of keeping only 56.7% / 40.0% of the 30 rows both definitions call positive. (c) THE CONTROL RULES OUT THE TRIVIAL EXPLANATION: AUC on those 117 disputed rows is 0.8454 raw / 0.8521 calibrated against v7's own 0.7218, and at bar 3.0 the student keeps 90% of the good while still removing 62% of the junk -- the two quantities move apart, so it learned a distinction rather than a lower scale. (d) CALIBRATION IS THE BETTER ARM after all, on every axis tied to the filter's purpose; the aggregate-recall band comparison was measuring in the wrong place, and this does not overturn 'not distinguishable' so much as relocate where the difference lives. (e) THE OP-POINT IS A VALUES CALL: under ADR-023 the inherited 4.5 is defensible, because moving to 4.0 buys 5 good articles and readmits 7 junk ones -- the wrong direction when a false positive costs a reader.
notes: CORRECTS EXP-016, which reported the fleet comparison as a finding rather than as an artifact of a changed definition. The corrected surfaces are filters/human_thriving/v8/STATUS.md, that filter's calibration_report.md, docs/evidence/2026-09-04-v8-probe-calibration/README.md, docs/TODO.md, memory/project_session_2026_09_04.md and H-V8-15 in memory/hypothesis-ledger.md. ⚠️ SCOPE: this shows v8 implements the definition the owner chose (#107, the class-A rulings). It does NOT show v8 is better than v7 in any absolute sense -- v7 is judged here against a target it was never trained on, so 0.7218 is a baseline and not a verdict on v7, and whether the new definition is right is an editorial judgement rather than a measurement. ⛔ STILL OPEN: the student under-learns class-A on the highest-scoring v7 rows -- 2 of 6 score ~5 against an oracle ~1, and both are rows v7 scored 6.28 and 6.57, i.e. the ones a reader is most likely to see. n=6; read the direction, not a rate. ⭐ Generalisable: an aggregate metric that POOLS the rows a change exists to demote with the rows it exists to keep cannot show whether the change worked, and will report a real improvement as 'not distinguishable'.

title: The fair test: can a vectorizer + MLP head trained AS A SCORER replace the student?
hypothesis: H-V8-17, raised by the owner. Every probe compared until now was trained as a SCREEN (--objective recall), which optimises the weighted average as a binary classifier and supervises the six dimensions through an auxiliary L1 weighted 0.1. That is the wrong objective for the claim 'you do not need the student'. Test a regression-objective probe at both encoder sizes.
subject: multilingual-e5-small and -large with --objective regression (L1 on the 6 oracle dimensions, checkpoint on val MAE), against the same four arms as EXP-018. One variable: same corpus, splits, --seed 42, GPU.

population.note: Decision rule fixed BEFORE the run: replacing the student requires the paired-bootstrap CI on delta-AUC to INCLUDE ZERO, not merely a small point difference.

decision_rationale: The student is NOT replaceable by the pre-registered rule -- in all four probe configurations the paired-bootstrap CI on delta-AUC excludes zero. But the owner's scepticism was substantially justified and the honest framing is a trade: the student finds ~6 more of 35 positives at EVERY surfacing volume (17% of the positive set) for 11.7x the compute. Whether that is worth paying is editorial, not statistical. THE OBJECTIVE MATTERED MORE THAN THE ENCODER: regression lifts e5-small from 0.8710 to 0.9035, past e5-large's recall-trained 0.9016 at a seventh of the compute, and with regression e5-large buys nothing on AUC. It also removes the inflation the recall objective causes (per-dim MAE 2.073 -> 0.762, bias +1.699 -> -0.298).
notes: ⛔ A DOCUMENTED PREDICTION DID NOT HOLD: train_probe.py and ADR-011 warn that regression 'will likely collapse to a floor predictor' below 25% positives; at 4.7% it did not collapse and beat the recall probe by 3.25 AUC points. ⚠️ That does NOT refute ADR-011 -- its claim is about regression AS A SCREEN, where collapse means unrecoverable Stage-1 false negatives, and this tested it AS A SCORER without ever selecting a threshold. The screen claim remains untested and needs an FN@MEDIUM+ at a selected threshold. ⚠️ CORRECTS AN EARLIER OBSERVATION THIS SESSION: I had noted the student on GPU (43.7 ms) beating the probe on CPU (47.2 ms) and concluded the two-stage design saved nothing -- an artefact of the wrong device. On GPU the probe is 11.7x cheaper. ⚠️ But the screen still barely earns its keep at the ADOPTED threshold for a different reason: routing is ~89%, so two-stage costs ~42.6 ms against 43.7 for student-on-everything, a 2.5% saving; at the probe's own 2.825 (routing ~52%) it would be ~26.5 ms. The hold-near-pass-through ruling is what makes the screen nearly free of benefit, knowingly, since no Stage-2 cost constraint was claimed. ⭐ My prediction held both halves this time, unlike EXP-018 two hours earlier.

title: Should the Stage-1 screen gate harder? What tightening costs and what it buys
hypothesis: Owner re-opened their own 2026-08-28 hold-near-pass-through ruling: 'this was supposed to be a needle-in-haystack filter, 89% pass-through does not sound needle to me'. Measure how hard the screen can go at a given FN budget, what tightening saves, and what it costs beyond compute.
subject: Four probes (recall/regression x e5-small/e5-large). Threshold selected on VAL at an FN budget, evaluated on TEST -- never both on the same split. Plus a closed-form cost model linear in the routing rate.

population.note: Threshold selection on 31 val positives; every conclusion here is provisional on that.

decision_rationale: NO CHANGE RECOMMENDED, and the 2026-08-28 ruling stands on its own stated premise. Harder gating IS available -- the shipped probe screens at 52.1% weighted instead of 89%, a 38% cut in scoring cost, for 1 of 35 test positives. But the ruling's reasoning was that no Stage-2 cost constraint was claimed, so buying FN risk gains nothing, and that reasoning is intact. THREE FINDINGS MAKE THIS MORE THAN A RESTATEMENT. (1) A BETTER RANKER DOES NOT BUY A SAFER SCREEN: regression e5-small ranks far better than the shipped probe (AUC 0.9035 vs 0.8710) and lands on essentially the same screen, 55.3%/1FN vs 56.5%/1FN. (2) THE 89% IS NOT SLACK -- it is what recall-safety costs at this ranking quality; 'needle-ness' is the 4.80% base rate, a different property from screen tightness. (3) TIGHTENING HAS A NON-COMPUTE COST NOBODY HAD WRITTEN DOWN: a screened-out row's PUBLISHED scores and tier are the probe's, so going 89% -> 52% takes the share of the corpus scored by the weaker instrument from 11% to 48% -- and the shipped recall probe is inflated +1.98 on the weighted average with per-dim MAE 3.4x the student's. If the screen is ever tightened it must be paired with a regression-objective probe, which removes the inflation (per-dim MAE 0.762, bias -0.298).
notes: ⛔ CORRECTS EXP-019, WHICH I OVERSTATED. I reported ADR-011's floor-collapse prediction as 'did not hold'. It holds. As a SCORER regression does not collapse; as a SCREEN, regression e5-large drops 6 of 35 positives -- 17% of the needles -- at 30.3% routing, exactly as ADR-011 describes. A probe can be the better scorer and the worse screen, and carrying a verdict between the roles is the error I made. ⚠️ A threshold giving 0% FN on VAL gave 1-6 FN on TEST for EVERY probe; threshold selection does not generalise at 31/35 positives, so any tightening is provisional on #141. ⚠️ Break-even routing is 52.7%: below it two-stage wins, above it e5-large-alone wins. The adopted 89% sits well above, which is the ONLY reason e5-large-alone looked competitive in EXP-018/019 -- tighten past ~53% and the two-stage architecture wins outright on cost and quality. ⚠️ All timings are b650-gpu, not gpu-server.

title: The op-point table: what the operating point separates, and what it cannot
hypothesis: Raised by the owner while weighing a cheaper Stage 2 ('i wouldn't want to lose too much on quality. Especially I do not want false positives'). No prior artifact computed ADR-023's own criterion -- specificity at the operating point -- for a PROBE arm; EXP-018/019/020 all ranked on AUC or average precision. Pre-stated expectation, from EXP-019's 'positives lost at matched volume': the best probe would cost false positives one-for-one against the student at the op-point. REFUTED for regression e5-large on the unweighted sample, CONFIRMED for regression e5-small.
subject: Six scoring arms over the 660-row human_thriving v8 test split, compared at MATCHED FLAG COUNT so FP = k - TP identically: student raw, student calibrated, and the recall- and regression-objective probes at e5-small and e5-large. Plus the gatekeeper applied/not applied per probe arm, the A/B/C/D cascades (A = gate->student, B = gate->e5-large, C = e5-large alone, D = e5-small alone) composed end to end, and a Horvitz-Thompson design-weighted arm. Arithmetic only on dumps retained from EXP-018/EXP-019 -- no GPU, no oracle, no new training.

population.note: k=17 and k=26 are what student_calibrated and student_raw flag at the literal 4.5 bar. 35 positives is the binding limit on every conclusion: re-selection bootstrap CIs run 4-9 articles wide. EVERY unweighted figure describes the SAMPLE; the split was drawn under a 25.1x design and the weighted arm disagrees.

WHAT STANDS: at k=17 the two regression probe arms differ by 6 articles with a re-selection-bootstrap CI of [+1,+9] excluding zero, while their whole-split AUCs are NOT separable (+0.0014, CI [-0.0448,+0.0476], P=0.523) -- the operating-point test separates them where the ranking metric cannot, which is a real argument for ADR-023's criterion. probe_reg_large's CI includes zero against the student at all eight k. WHAT WAS RETRACTED BEFORE COMMIT, by a four-lens /review-changes that ran AFTER the whole mechanical battery went green and found none of it: (1) 'AUC would have picked the wrong arm' was a coin flip published as an ordering (P=0.523) -- and it does not generalise, because AUC separates the student from probe_reg_large (P=0.995) where the op-point test cannot, so 'the op-point test is underpowered' is not excluded; (2) 'the gate buys nothing, identical TP at all eight k' was FORCED -- the smallest k at which a screened row could enter is 140 against a grid stopping at 60, the first working rule exactly; what stands independently is 0 of 35 positives screened and the 85.7% break-even, which needs no data; (3) the paired bootstrap froze its top-k masks and emitted a zero-width 95% CI, now replaced by a re-selection bootstrap with a null control; (4) every figure was UNWEIGHTED on a 25.1x design-weighted split -- weighted, the student leads probe_reg_large at every share tested (0.529 vs 0.478 of the positive mass at the weighted positive rate). title: Four claim-shape checks, and the design-weighted arm of the phase-8 trade table
hypothesis: Not a hypothesis test. Pre-stated: each check must be seeded with a true positive and shown to FIRE, because a check that never catches anything is indistinguishable from one that works. It caught six real sites on the first run.
subject: scripts/verification/check_claim_shapes.py -- (a) a no-difference-over-a-grid claim must publish the range over which it could have differed; (b) a published zero-width interval is a defect signal, one printed exemption for a declared null control; (c) a quantified comparative ordering needs a band or p-value in its paragraph; (d) an analysis reading a design-weighted population must read the weights or declare in writing why not. The trade columns are conditional on the v7-surfaced partition, which is why they are the stabler instrument for this decision. The four checks are kept and wired into memory/MEMORY.md's verify annotations. title: The ADR-021 deploy gate for human_thriving v8, on a CUDA re-score
hypothesis: Phase 8's last open action. Two questions, pre-stated. (1) Does the deploy gate's verdict depend on the DEVICE? Every v8 accuracy number was CPU-measured while production serves on GPU (#104), uplifting v7's CPU->CUDA term is max |delta| 0.1956 with 3 flips at the same 4.5 bar, and EXP-015 saw CUDA give 18 TP against CPU's 17 -- so the expectation was a small number of flips. REFUTED for v8: zero flips, identical confusion matrices. (2) NM#319, which the op-point ruling explicitly did not settle: does v8's distribution sit below NexusMind's enrichment gate at normalized 4.0? Answered structurally rather than by v8's own CDF, which does not exist yet.
subject: The 660-row human_thriving v8 held-out test split, re-scored on CUDA with gpu-server's production pins, then judged by scripts/gate/ground_truth_gate.py against the oracle labels at the ruled op-point 4.50 (calibrated). Both arms from ONE forward pass. Compared row-by-row against the 2026-09-04 CPU dump of the same split, same weights, same script. Plus a read of uplifting v7's production output as the proxy for what percentile normalization does to the enrichment gate.

population.nm319_proxy: uplifting v7 production output on sadalsuud
population.note: The gate rates are UNWEIGHTED sample rates on a 25.1x design that over-samples positives. The NM#319 numbers are v7's, not v8's: v8 has no production population and no fitted CDF, so the SHARE will differ and only the mechanism transfers. All 18,041 surfaced v7 rows are stage_used=stage2, so raw_weighted_average is a Gemma score there and not a probe estimate.

decision_rationale: KEPT: this is v8's deploy-gate number and it closes phase 8's last action -- recall 0.343 / specificity 0.992 at 4.50 calibrated, 660 held-out oracle rows, written to filters/human_thriving/v8/ground_truth_gate.json with automatic input sha256s and a hand-written provenance block. The re-score was NOT wasted by its own null result: the CPU dumps were on disk and would have run, and nothing but the measurement could say whether v8's device term reached the bar the way v7's did. Two things the gate does NOT decide: calibrated vs raw are not distinguishable under the #95 band (all three bands overlap), and v8's recall does not belong beside the fleet's 0.59-0.72 because v7 and v8 do not share a positive class. NM#319 answered in two regimes: before Phase E, score_scale_factor 1.0 passes raw through and every surfaced article clears the 4.0 gate; after Phase E, anchoring puts the op-point at normalized 0.0 by construction, and on v7 today that leaves 40% of surfaced articles silently un-enriched. Phase E itself is BLOCKED and the ordering is the reason: the fitter reads NexusMind production output, sadalsuud has no human_thriving at all, so normalization comes after deployment as it did for solutions v6. ⭐ AND IT REFUTED A RECORDED EXPLANATION: STATUS.md attributed EXP-015's raw recall of 0.514 (18 TP of 35) against this gate's 0.486 (17) to 'a device difference ... the CPU->CUDA 0.1956 term landing near the bar'. The device gives 0 flips on this split, and applying or removing the gatekeeper and clamp moves 0 rows across 4.5 on either device. The difference is the DTYPE, i.e. the program: the production inference path holds 342 bfloat16 parameters against 364 float32 with the score head in bf16 (read off the loaded object), while eval_ht_v8.py forces torch_dtype=torch.float32 and reaches the model through PeftModel.from_pretrained at batch 8. Production serves bf16, so 17 is production's number and 18 is the fp32 arm's. A dismissal is a claim: 'it's the device' survived because it named a real, measured, plausible term on a filter whose remaining risk was a device caveat. ⛔ THE REVIEW ALSO CHANGED THE ARTIFACT, not just the write-up: three blockers were in code added by this change, one of them a hole in the very tests written to prove the feature, and all three were invisible to a fully green mechanical battery.
review: Five-lens /review-changes (guarantee-preservation, reachability, claim-verification, adversarial, doc-accuracy) on a tree that had already passed the whole mechanical battery: 715 tests, doc-claims, claim-shapes, the registry checker and both budget guards. VERIFICATION IS NOT REVIEW, 6th session running -- the battery found none of the following. BLOCKERS, all in code added by this change: (1) the provenance carry-over reintroduced the very defect it was written to prevent, one layer up -- a rerun on a different dump/device/checkpoint kept prose describing the old run, beside a freshly correct `inputs` block that made it look newly attributed; now stamped with a fingerprint of the inputs it described, with three states (matches / UNVERIFIED / STALE), because conflating the last two makes the warning fire on every rerun. (2) THE FLAGSHIP TEST HOLE: none of the four new tests varied the SCORES between the two gate runs, so mutating `report['provenance'] = prior['provenance']` into `report.update(prior)` -- which reverts every freshly computed metric to the previous file's -- PASSED ALL FOUR. A retrained model's gate report would have kept the old model's recall. Found by the adversarial lens mutating the real file. (3) A `--config` that cannot be read fell through load_scoring_spec's bare `except` to nature_recovery v4's constants and printed a full table at someone else's operating point (threshold 4.0, gatekeeper 3.5), exit 0; now refused. WARNINGS: the dump script's own Usage docstring still taught both hazards this change exists to remove (no --require-device, --out-dir under /tmp); the dtype conclusion overclaimed -- three differences (dtype, adapter loader, batch size) were named and NONE isolated, so it is now stated as the leading candidate and registered as H-V8-23 with a falsifier; 'mutation-tested three ways' read as more coverage than existed. doc-accuracy verified every cross-file figure against a mounted NexusMind checkout (82 cycles, the filtered/ directory listing, production_scorer.py:17-18, article_fetcher.py:1374, app.yaml:278 all byte-exact) and found one pre-existing stale sentence 8 lines from text this commit edited ('it has no base_scorer.py yet ... 4.5 is currently a documentation value'), now corrected. reachability and guarantee-preservation returned clean, and confirmed ground_truth_gate.json has NO reader in either repo -- it is evidence, not config.
notes: b650 ran BOTH passes, so no cross-box term is measured here and CUDA-to-CUDA against gpu-server remains unmeasured. b650's ~/llm-distillery is not a git checkout: four files on the scoring path had drifted and were synced from the repo before the CUDA pass, with the pre-sync copies kept at ~/llm-distillery/.presync_backup_20260906/ -- the differences were docstrings plus one off-path argument, checked file by file and recorded in DUMP_MANIFEST.md, which is why the CPU pass is still comparable as a device measurement.

title: Retrain human_thriving v8 under a real commit — does removing the provenance exception cost accuracy?
hypothesis: The shipped v8 adapter was built by a tree `git commit --amend` orphaned, so no commit names it. The owner rejected recording an exception ('no exception, i want this system to be harmonized'). Retrain under a commit on main with identical data, seed, hyperparameters and selection metric, then re-run the ADR-021 gate. Question: does the harmonized checkpoint cost measurable accuracy?
subject: google/gemma-3-1b-pt + LoRA, 6 epochs, batch 8, lr 2e-5, max_length 512, seed 42, --select-metric recall_medium, medium_threshold 4.5 from base_scorer.py TIER_THRESHOLDS. Identical to EXP-015 except that train.py now stamps and enforces git provenance. b650-gpu, CUDA, venv-prodparity.
oracle: deepseek-chat (labels only; no oracle calls in this experiment)

population.note: Splits identical to EXP-015 (test.jsonl sha256 e361b5175c66...). The 660 rows are a 25.1x design-weighted draw; every rate here is unweighted and describes the SPLIT.

decision_rationale: Kept, and the accuracy question came back NOT DISTINGUISHABLE. All four #95 bands overlap with the superseded checkpoint's (recall, precision, specificity, F1), so under the owner's 2026-08-06 rule the two models are not distinguishable whatever the point estimates say -- and the point estimates do all move adversely (precision 0.706 -> 0.550, FP 5 -> 9). THE HARM-WEIGHTED VIEW IS WHY THAT IS NOT ALARMING: classified by the oracle's own scope_verdict, 6 of the 9 false positives are `in_scope` -- thriving stories scored just under 4.5 that the student put just over -- so genuinely off-lens is 3 of 20 (off-lens precision 0.850 vs 0.882) and category errors are 1, the SAME as before. The apparent precision collapse is boundary disagreement, not junk reaching readers. The checkpoint also differs from its predecessor by more than run-to-run noise: recall_medium SATURATED in EXP-015 so the tie-break kept epoch 4, and it did not saturate here, so selection chose epoch 5 outright (#144).
notes: THE KEEPER IS THE MECHANISM, NOT THE MODEL. train.py now RESOLVES AND ENFORCES provenance BEFORE the ~100-minute run -- a gap discovered after a long run is a long run you cannot cite -- and check_training_provenance.py re-reads the stamp LATER, which is the only time an amend or a gc can have orphaned the commit. A stamp is a claim about the past; reachability is a property of now. SECOND: b650's ~/llm-distillery was a partial rsync, not a checkout, and its training/train.py was the PRE-FIX version missing 176 lines of checkpoint-selection machinery that main says trained the old artifact -- so the provenance was not merely unrecorded, the box did not hold the code the record named. It is now a real checkout with 0 tracked-file drift; its uplifting v7 config/normalization/base_scorer had also drifted, and main was byte-identical to sadalsuud, so the checkout moved b650 TOWARD production. THIRD, an honest limit: this buys TRACEABILITY, NOT BIT-REPRODUCIBILITY. The run is not deterministic at this seed (EXP-015 saw 0.5601 vs 0.5605 on rerun; epoch 1 here was 0.7728 against 0.7773), so re-running 64b469d yields a near-identical but different model. FOURTH: the first calibration fit ran on b650 at 64b469d, BEFORE the device-print landed at 0d7115a, so it could not confirm its own device; it was re-run at 0d7115a and printed declared=cuda parameters=cuda:0, reproducing the numbers exactly. FIFTH, incidental and worth a guard: labels_v84_merged.jsonl carries TWO SCHEMAS in one file -- 6,130 rows with scalar dimensions and 456 (the v8.4 re-labelled ones) with {'score': x}. Naive a[dim]*weight crashes; naive .get(dim, 0) would silently score them ZERO.
